sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Aesthetik is a growing façade contractor with an increasingly material solar business, but it is not presently a clean low-P/E investment. FY2026 legacy-group revenue rose78.5% to₹118.21crore while PAT rose26.2% to₹7.13crore. Reported CFO₹14.86crore includes₹13.73crore borrowing inflow; removing that leaves₹1.13crore before a further₹0.95crore operating-asset classification adjustment. The three-year cash picture is weak despite accounting profit. [S1–S3]

The investment perimeter is also changing radically. A sanctioned La Reliant merger provides for51,698,871new shares versus17,220,175legacy shares. The effective ROC filing, actual allotment, current target accounts and remaining project funding were not verified by cutoff. The available September2025 pro forma includes₹657.41crore goodwill. A bank letter described by management as in-principle financing expressly says it is only an expression of intent, not acceptance or sanction. Do not use legacy earnings with a post-merger denominator, or combined earnings with legacy shares. Current combined BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS where those missing inputs are material. L=1 is independently supportable. Classification: evidence/funding hold, not a buy or a proven compounder. [S4–S5,S10–S13]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Cutoff20October2026. Identity verified: Aesthetik Engineers Limited, INE0TSF01011, NSE Emerge, listed16August2024. Legacy audited FY2026 results are consolidated Ind AS; La Reliant's underlying accounts use Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, with merger pro-forma adjustments. No FY2026 full annual report was found on the issuer site; the AGM was formally extended and scheduled28November, so absence is not described as an unapproved overdue AGM. [S1,S3–S7]

Latest observed official trade is15October close₹71.80, not an invented19October close. Legacy issued-capital market value is₹123.64crore. Scheme total shares would be68,919,046, but this is not certified actual issued capital at cutoff. G1 integrity: conditional, with documented board-process and bank-statement discrepancies, not a finding of fraud. G2 financial comparability: unresolved for current combined perimeter, with explicit historical cash reclassification. G3 funding: unresolved for the large new project; no observed default is asserted. G4 execution: highly illiquid but a coarse L=1 is supported, not automatically untradeable. Historical inputs Medium confidence; current combined valuation inputs Low; forecast uncertainty High. [S1,S4–S5,S10–S14]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors supported across the uncertainty: GOV4, MOAT4, DUR4 and CASH2, all Medium input confidence. Current REV, CAP, BAL, EXEC and EARN are NS because the transformative combined financial perimeter and actual implementation/funding are not established. This is not a downgrade for missing promotional information: the prospective share issue is roughly three times legacy shares and the financing commitment is not demonstrated. Q thereforeNS; R,D and P areNS for a current whole-company investment case; L1 is supported independently.

BQS known weighted sum2.20,coverage60%,mathematical missing-data bound2.60–6.20. GQS known sum1.00,coverage30%,bound1.70–8.00 before the persistent weak-cash cap5. IAS known sum0.10,coverage10%,bound1.00–9.10. No weights are redistributed and no point composite is ranked. These are missing-data bounds, not confidence intervals.

A separately labeled legacy-business diagnostic would use GOV4/MOAT4/REV8/DUR4/CAP4/CASH2/BAL3/EXEC5/EARN4: BQS4.28 and GQS5.40 before cash cap,5.00 after. REV uses FY2023–26 standalone revenue40.0098→94.4071crore,33.13%CAGR, with short-history ceiling8; it is not a combined-company growth score. This illustration is excluded from the current company scores and rankings. Changing legacy GOV and CAP by±1 shifts illustrative BQS±0.32; it does not resolve the missing perimeter. [S1–S5]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
The legacy business designs, engineers, fabricates, tests and installs building façades, glazing, cladding, aluminium windows/doors and related envelope systems. Customer purchase decisions depend on design specification, execution reliability, safety, installation quality and price. Revenue is project/work-contract driven; collections can lag billing and inventory procurement, with retentions and advances affecting cash. The FY2025 annual report describes74,000sqft Howrah and20,000sqft Mumbai facilities. These are floor areas, not throughput or annual revenue capacity. [S1–S2]

Solisys became wholly owned inFebruary2025, Aesthetik Renewables is a subsidiary, and glass-processing interests add integration complexity. FY2026 auditor reports subsidiary revenue₹21.84crore for Solisys and₹3.73crore for Renewables, not amounts to add again to consolidated sales. Uday Tuff appears as associate. La Reliant adds aluminium extrusion and a proposed Surat solar-frame/module project, not merely more façade orders. These different economics require intercompany elimination and accounting alignment. FY2024 IPO customer tables already show sales to La Reliant entities, so simply adding both companies' revenue would be wrong. [S2–S4]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Mechanism: design-and-install experience and specification/customer qualification can lower execution risk for a buyer. Evidence: a lengthy operating record, named institutional/developer customers and completed product capabilities. Durability: relationships can support repeat work, but procurement remains competitive and project specific. Failure mode: a capable engineering/fabrication competitor can win the next project on price, quality or delivery; there is no evidenced network effect or irreplaceable proprietary system. MOAT4 reflects useful capability without proven durable excess pricing or cost economics. [S1–S2]

FY2024 top10 customers represented81.05% of sales; Infosys alone24.69%. About86.5% of revenue then came from West Bengal. These are dated concentration measures, not claims about FY2026. Mumbai expansion broadens access, but no current customer-concentration or market-share denominator was verified. Reputed customers and an₹83.73crore order book dated1April2025 do not establish a moat. A new solar-frame/module plant would enter contestable manufacturing markets; customer EOIs are not exclusive supply contracts. [S1–S2,S4]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Standalone revenue was₹25.7391/40.0098/60.7203/57.8827/94.4071crore in FY2022–26. Five-year and10-year comparable CAGRs cannot be established from the inspected series; the preferred available three-year window is FY2023–26,33.13%, not a cherry-picked latest-year rate. Consolidated FY2024–26 revenue60.7203→66.2358→118.2111 adds₹5.52crore then₹51.98crore, but subsidiary perimeter changes mean it is not all demonstrated organic growth. Parent revenue itself declined in FY2025 before rebounding63.1% in FY2026. [S1–S3]

FY2026 group H1/H2 revenue₹37.7064/80.5047crore versus FY2025H2₹40.4307crore. H2 growth≈99.1% came with PAT₹3.6227crore versus₹4.8849crore a year earlier: a much lower margin, not seamless operating leverage. A price/volume/mix bridge was not disclosed. Gross value added, calculated as revenue less material cost adjusted for WIP, is₹31.1583crore in FY2026 versus₹20.0345crore FY2025; value-added growth≈55.5% trails sales growth. La Reliant's FY2027₹843.34crore management projection is excluded from achieved revenue and REV. Current combined organic REV remainsNS. [S1,S3–S4]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Façade penetration, western-India work and integrated glass supply provide a real but contestable runway. The annual report's dated backlog and the merger notice's₹45crore Mumbai doors/windows orders are not a reconciled current backlog: intake, execution, cancellations, advances and final margins were not supplied. DUR4 balances accessible demand against the unproven funding/customer conversion of the much larger new manufacturing plan. [S1,S4]

Legacy three-year financing-side incremental-ROIC proxy is approximately11.4% on standalone normalized EBIT after26%analyst tax, using FY2023 equity+debt−reportedcash₹15.658crore and FY2026₹60.1714crore. This is around/below a12–16%nominal INR cost-of-capital sensitivity, not proven high-return compounding. It includes new facilities and does not isolate commissioned cohorts; it is not applied to the merged company. Full acquisition capital including goodwill must be considered before assigning combined CAP. [S1–S3]

La Reliant's FY2025 consolidated revenue₹159.86crore/PAT₹7.11crore accompanied CFO−₹5.67crore. Its September2025 equity increase reflects a substantial capital raise, not only retained earnings. The bank preliminary proposal has project cost₹195.68crore, TL₹130crore, new WC₹50crore with LC/BG sublimits, and₹18crore takeover of an existing line. None is proved committed/drawn by that letter. Cost minus hypothetical TL is₹65.68crore before WC/DSRA/fees, not a verified remaining shortfall, because actual expenditure and prior equity deployment are unknown. No earlier equity proceeds are added a second time. [S4]

Latest contrary evidence: the target's own current Devron page, inspected20October, now markets a dedicated Surat solar-frame line rated4,000MT/month and says commissioning October2026. The5October-indexed profile describes automated integration, while the homepage advertises54,000MTPA across the business. These are management capacity/timetable claims, not certified achieved production or funding. The page explicitly labels much of its footage as Kolkata; it cannot prove Surat completion. The9.5GW figure is the module-production equivalent supported by frames, not9.5GW of module manufacturing. This updated October timetable must be distinguished from the earlier bank proposal's June2026COD; no actual start date or audited ramp was verified. [S15–S17]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The FY2025 secretarial report records omitted board notices/agenda/draft minutes to two directors and absent explanatory notes in some notices, plus SS2 discrepancies. Management acknowledges lapses and says processes were strengthened; independent effectiveness has not been verified. CARO reports bank current-asset statements above books in all four quarters: June₹19.6514versus17.8497crore and September19.6253versus17.7064crore are the larger differences. These are disclosed control concerns, not a finding of fabricated assets or fraud. The auditor also reports no observed loan default or reported fraud for its period and functioning audit-trail software. Both sides matter. [S1]

FY2025 director remuneration≈₹0.6825crore and related rent₹1.26crore compare with standalone PAT₹5.2808crore; related Uday Glass loan₹3.50crore plus accrued interest and rent deposits require capital-allocation scrutiny. Management's arm's-length statement is not independent pricing proof. March2026 promoters held69.57%, with no pledge/NDU/other encumbrance declared then; this does not certify October ownership or pledges. The employee trust held96,000already-issued shares and21,198ESOPs were outstanding; settlement terms are needed before treating options as additional issued shares. [S1,S9]

September19 appointment of Vaani Agarwal, daughter of the MD and executive director and granddaughter of the whole-time director, increases family representation. Priyanka Jalan and Abhishek Sawaria resigned citing outside opportunities; no audit dispute is inferred. May23 auditor-change headlines concern internal/secretarial appointments, not proof a statutory auditor resigned. ROC-approved AGM extension is distinguished from noncompliance. [S6–S7]

The scheme dilutes legacy ownership to24.99% of enlarged shares while adding a different business, and projects promoter ownership74.16%. Valuer and fairness reports exist, but the valuer expressly does not assure management projections. The bank's18August2025 letter expressly leaves sanction to later due diligence and discretion; its contents are stronger evidence than the management shorthand 'in-principle sanction.' June2026 COD was a target, not verified achieved or conclusively missed. Execution is therefore unresolved for the new perimeter rather than scored as an invented failure. Similar-name regulatory hits in the pack were expressly denied as unrelated by the issuer; they are not attributed to its directors. [S4–S5]

Latest contrary evidence: the target's own current Devron page, inspected20October, now markets a dedicated Surat solar-frame line rated4,000MT/month and says commissioning October2026. The5October-indexed profile describes automated integration, while the homepage advertises54,000MTPA across the business. These are management capacity/timetable claims, not certified achieved production or funding. The page explicitly labels much of its footage as Kolkata; it cannot prove Surat completion. The9.5GW figure is the module-production equivalent supported by frames, not9.5GW of module manufacturing. This updated October timetable must be distinguished from the earlier bank proposal's June2026COD; no actual start date or audited ramp was verified. [S15–S17]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Legacy group FY2024/FY2025/FY2026: revenue₹60.7203/66.2358/118.2111crore; reported PAT₹5.0088/5.6479/7.1250crore; core EBITDA excluding other income approximately₹7.7081/8.6267/12.0415crore. Core EBITDA margin therefore12.69%/13.02%/10.19%, while PAT margin8.25%/8.53%/6.03%. FY2026 EBIT-interest cover is roughly5.6times on other-income-excluded EBIT, not a liquidity guarantee. Other income₹0.8579crore and associate profit₹0.0458crore should not be mistaken for façade cash generation. Applying25–28%tax to FY2026PBT less other income gives normalized operating-profit-after-tax sensitivity₹6.22–6.48crore, excluding associate earnings; this is an analyst normalization, not restated statutory PAT. [S1–S3]

Cash bridge: FY2025 annual CFO₹2.6110crore includes₹4.3430crore short-term borrowing change, leaving−₹1.7320crore. FY2026 comparative reclassifies₹0.0613crore between long/short financing and presents CFO₹2.6723crore with₹4.4043crore borrowing inflow: the same−₹1.7320crore after normalization. This difference is reconciled, not called missing cash. FY2026 CFO₹14.8559crore explicitly includes₹13.7283crore borrowings. The resulting₹1.1276crore upper operating measure falls to≈₹0.1780crore if the₹0.9496crore increase in other current assets is moved from the investing 'other non-current assets' line to operations; the latter line equals actual NCA release₹0.0627crore less that current-asset increase. This is an accounting-placement adjustment, not a claim cash disappeared. [S1,S3]

FY2024 later annual CFO−₹2.4986crore becomes−₹2.0572crore after removing a negative₹0.4414crore borrowing movement. Three-year normalized CFO is about−₹3.61crore, or−0.20times cumulative PAT₹17.78crore; even without the FY2026₹0.95crore adjustment it remains negative. Cash capex₹2.3729/11.0421/12.2937crore produces FCF proxies−₹4.4301/−₹12.7741/−₹12.1157crore. These are before separately classified financing interest and do not add loan advances, deposits or investments back as distributable cash. Earlier IPO FY2024 cash-flow presentation differs materially and has a closing-cash mismatch; later audited annual comparative is used, with the original retained as a comparability warning. [S1–S3]

March2026 inventory₹26.1593crore is up179%; receivables₹17.3988crore fell7.7%. Closing inventory days rise≈51.7→80.8 while receivable days fall≈103.9→53.7, using annual sales consistently. Better debtor collection is a positive contrary fact, but inventory absorbs more cash. Payables rise₹5.7414→11.4148crore; supplier funding is not customer cash. FY2026 aged balances and exact cash restrictions await full notes. FY2025 reported cash₹2.9404crore included₹2.68crore deposits; other financial assets₹3.9053crore were mainly deposits, not free cash. The model excludes those assets and tests cash0–₹2.9888crore. [S1,S3]

Legal exposures remain separate from liabilities actually payable: service-tax demand₹0.8240crore plus roughly₹0.8250crore penalty and interest, appeal pending in the inspected disclosures; a FY2025annual supplier dispute around₹0.3447crore; the merger notice adds GST demand/interest/penalty with an appeal rejected11March2026 and intended further appeal, and La Reliant income-tax demand₹4.5775crore under appeal. No later final disposition was verified. The scheme's statement that pending proceedings transfer is relevant, but this is not an adverse legal verdict. [S1,S4–S5]

Model review, 20 October 2026: the legacy diagnostic now deducts ₹0.0646 crore opening noncurrent provisions from terminal equity. These provisions were omitted from the previous diagnostic. The already reserved ₹0.4110 crore other noncurrent liability is retained against cash rather than described as immediately due. This is our model correction, not a new issuer failure. Opening current provisions ₹0.0752 crore and other current liabilities ₹4.55 crore remain in the broad operating working-capital stock, without a second settlement charge; no granular FY2026 notes establish a separate additional claim. The ₹0.5546 crore net tax asset is neither monetised nor netted again. Core cash gaps and score/gate conclusions are unchanged; the optimistic maintenance-only annualised return changes from 2.2187% to 2.2093%.

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the latest observed15October₹71.80, legacy issued-share market cap₹123.64crore implies about17.35times FY2026PAT. Legacy EV using reported borrowings₹24.8671crore and all reported cash₹2.9888crore is₹145.52crore,≈12.08times core EBITDA. Excluding unverified cash raises EV. These are legacy-scope cross-checks, not a combined-company bargain claim. At an unchanged quote the full scheme share count would imply about₹494.84crore equity value; a pro-forma goodwill asset is not cash backing. [S3–S5,S10–S11]

An explicit five-year legacy cash model is attached to the audit. Base growth12/10/8/6/5%, EBITDA margin10.2%before cash lease, incremental WC28%of added revenue, maintenance₹2crore growing5%, growth capex₹3/2/1/0/0crore, no new financing. Bull growth25/20/15/12/10%,11.5%margin,25%incremental WC, higher capex; bear−25/0/3/5/5%,7%margin,35%incremental WC plus collection/inventory/funding shocks. Opening WC uses actual balances, not a ratio applied backward. Terminal8/12/15times NOPAT, debt/cash bridge,26%tax,1%entry/exit cost and no dividends. [S3; analyst assumptions]

With all reported cash provisionally usable, base misses the analyst₹1crore cash buffer by₹0.109crore but never has negative cash; bull requires₹4.98crore actual incremental cash and bear₹23.31crore. These are scenario funding deficiencies, not observed defaults. No qualified IRR is assigned to cases breaching their funding condition. Maintenance-only sensitivity funds and yields only about2.2%annualized, but keeping the same growth after removing growth capex is deliberately optimistic, not the base forecast. Terminal legacy values are conditional illustrations, not price targets. Exact lease/cash/loan maturity notes and ESOP settlement are additional model limitations.

A current combined IRR cannot be certified: the only combined accounts are a September2025unaudited pro forma, with share-capital suspense, acquisition-date adjustments and substantial goodwill. Updated target cash/debt, actual project expenditure, committed credit and implementation dates are missing. No annualization of that pro forma is called actual FY2026, and no mixed denominator is used. R/IAS remainNS for these material reasons, not because a live bid–ask spread is absent. [S4–S5]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Legacy adverse chain: project delays and lower margins combine with15%inventory loss,15%receivable loss,30extra collection days and withdrawal of25%of March short-term funding. There is no automatic working-capital release from falling sales. The modeled cash deficit is₹23.31crore before any new financing; distressed equity raising or impaired liquidation could permanently dilute owners. This is an explicit stress, not a forecast insolvency allegation. [S3; analyst assumptions]

Merger adverse chain: the new plant is delayed or fails qualification, nonbinding EOIs do not become orders, lender due diligence does not produce committed finance, and the group must fund capex/WC after issuing a large equity consideration. Full acquisition economics can disappoint even if book goodwill remains unimpaired initially. Conversely, verified bank sanction/disbursements, commissioning and good cash collections could improve this case materially; those facts must be observed, not assumed. Tax/dispute exposures add potential claims, but no final liability is invented. [S4–S5]

Trading itself adds permanent-loss/execution risk. Conditional all60-session median turnover₹1.44525lakh/day implies≈69.2sessions to exit₹5lakh at5%participation; observed44-day-only median₹3.06775lakh still implies≈32.6sessions. The1000share lot costs₹71,800at the stale quote. A displayed price is not evidence a position can be sold there. [S10–S13]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold or tenfold wealth is not supported merely by the management's proposed solar turnover. At the legacy share count and unchanged shares,5×/10× the₹71.80quote means equity values around₹618/1,236crore. At12times terminal NOPAT and₹20crore net debt, this would require roughly₹53/105crore NOPAT. At7%NOPAT margin, revenue would need approximately₹760/1,500crore, far above the legacy linked scenarios and demanding much more funded capital. These are algebraic hurdles, not forecasts.

Fivefold in5/10years requires38.0%/17.5%annualized; tenfold requires58.5%/25.9%, before friction. After the merger the denominator and acquired obligations both change, so the legacy hurdle cannot be reused unadjusted. The pro-forma acquisition, solar expansion and cash-conversion record do not establish a per-share5×/10× path. No probability is invented for one. [S3–S5,S10]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before any investment upgrade: obtain certified ROC effective-date filings and actual allotment/listing/capital reconciliation; tie every quoted valuation to that perimeter. Obtain latest La Reliant audited results and full combined acquisition accounting, including goodwill, intercompany eliminations, liabilities and tax treatment. Request actual project cost spent/remaining, bank final sanction and draw schedule, equity already deployed, DSRA/collateral and commissioning/customer qualification evidence. [S4–S5]

Next results: reconcile CFO excluding borrowings and operating items in CFI; track inventory days, debtor ageing/retentions, deposits/restrictions, loans and supplier finance. Require cash conversion to improve without fresh borrowings presented as operations. Check whether H2 margin compression recurs. Read FY2026annual/AGM materials and subsequent shareholding/ESOP disclosures; verify board-process remediation and bank-book reconciliations. Observe cash against debt maturities, not just EPS. [S1–S3,S6–S9]

Market implementation: refresh actual traded date, lot/band/surveillance and60-session mean/median; do not replace absent sessions with guaranteed liquidity. No automatic buy trigger is attached to a lower price while perimeter/funding remain unresolved. A deteriorating credit event, failed project financing, growing aged balances or unfavorable dilution would worsen the thesis even if accounting sales grow. [S10–S14]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Deep evidence-led review with a current-perimeter and funding hold. Historical business is a capable but cash-intensive project operator, not yet a demonstrated high-return compounder. Current combined composite scores areNS; do not rank a legacy diagnostic as the present merged business. L1 denotes severe execution illiquidity even though named surveillance categories are not active in the inspected NSE indicators.

For a new position, defer a positive investment conclusion until financial scope, merger shares and committed financing reconcile. This is not a universal sell instruction for an existing holder and is not an allegation of fraud/default. The actionable research conclusion is specific: an apparently modest legacy P/E cannot settle a transformative, incompletely funded acquisition case. [S1–S5,S10–S13]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources include the IPO prospectus, FY2025annual report, audited FY2026results, complete scheme explanation and selected underlying audit/valuation/financing annexures, JulyNCLT order, Septemberboard/AGM extension and Marchshareholding. Search results were used for discovery, not substituted for the underlying bank letter or accounts. Official NSE quote/liquidity/security/surveillance data are separately dated. The supplied CSV snapshot has no date and is not treated as verified current market data. [S1–S14]

Material open questions: last ROC filing/effectiveness and actual allotment; latest target/combined financial statements; final bank sanction and disbursements; actual remaining project spend and customer contracts; cash restrictions, debt/lease maturities, FY2026ageing and complete ESOP terms; post-March ownership/pledges and later legal dispositions. The issuer's scheme 'Additional Document' link was unavailable; its shareholding page inspected stopped atMarch2026. Absence of a discovered filing does not prove an event never happened. No inaccessible source is presented as read.

Analyst assumptions are identified in the model rather than labeled verified: revenue/margin paths, incremental WC, capex, normalized tax, economic depreciation, cash bounds, amortization, terminal multiples, stress losses and execution costs. The model does not add IPO or target equity cash twice, does not count loan/takeover limits as free cash, and does not average share-count scopes. Frozen earlier delivery snapshots are unchanged.

A final check of La Reliant's own investor page recovered only FY2025/September2025 financial statements and pre-implementation scheme documents, plus a5October2026 Devron profile. Current commissioning/capacity statements are retained as contrary management evidence, not excluded because they are promotional. They do not resolve actual allotment, current accounts or final financing. [S15–S17]
